app.title: Cat-O-Fit · Training plans for the whole family
app.description: Training plans for the whole family – plan, train and review races and programmes, with nutrition, cycle and lab values in view. On your own server.

workoutMode.discardInfo: The {time} minutes you’ve trained so far won’t be saved.
workoutMode.hintNoLock: Keep your screen unlocked – signals pause while it’s locked, but the clock keeps counting correctly.
workoutMode.hintNoVibrate: Your device can’t vibrate here – signals come as sounds (on iPhone only with the silent switch off).
workoutMode.hintNoWakeLock: Keeping the screen awake isn’t supported here – turn off auto-lock for your workout.
workoutMode.drinkBanner: Drink break – take a few sips
workoutMode.restHint: Breathe and get ready for the next set
workoutMode.quitQuestion: Do you want to finish your workout and log it?
workoutMode.noSuggestions: No suggestions – add exercises with “+” on the exercise screen.

exerciseLib.subtitle: {n} exercises · {w} follow-along workouts
exerciseLib.disclaimer: Symbolic animations – they show the basic movement and rhythm, no substitute for individual coaching.

calendar.dragTip: Tip: drag a session by its handle ⠿ to another day – or tap the handle and pick a date.

returnLock.one: No step-ups until {count} day after your illness or injury.
returnLock.other: No step-ups until {count} days after your illness or injury.

why.warning: Warning signs come before plan upkeep and step-ups.
why.boost: No warning signs, load within your usual range.
why.plan: No warning signs – now it’s about your plan.

triage.lowerFixed: “{title}” is a fixed appointment – make the other session easier or move it instead.
triage.moveLower: Move “{title}” or make it easier – recovery belongs between two hard efforts.
triage.tooManyHard: {count} hard sessions in one week – 2–3 are usually enough to recover between efforts.
triage.softenLeast: Turn the least important one (“{title}”) into an easy run – quality over quantity.
triage.doubleHard: Two hard sessions on the same day ({day}).
triage.bothFixed: Both are fixed appointments – keep the day after deliberately easy and, where you can, take the intensity out of the second one.
triage.allHardFixed: The hard sessions are fixed appointments – keep your easy days really easy.
triage.noRest: No day off training this week.
triage.noRestSuggest: Plan at least one rest day – recovery is when your body adapts.
triage.doubleHardSuggest: Spread them over two days – each effort works better and you recover properly.

whatif.b2b: This puts two hard days back to back.
whatif.sameLoadB2b: Your weekly load stays the same ({load}), but this puts two hard days back to back. Make recovery a priority.
whatif.bitHarder: This week gets a bit harder ({load}).
whatif.littleEffect: Hardly any effect on your weekly load ({load}).

priorityHint.A: A – season highlight: your plan builds up to this day.
priorityHint.B: B – important race: run it seriously, without a full plan leading up to it.
priorityHint.C: C – build-up or fun race: take it along as a training stimulus.

events.raceTodayNoPlan: It’s race day – too late for a training plan now. Good luck!

events.noPlanYet: There’s no plan for this race yet. Create a periodised training plan up to race day – matched to your level and your running days.
events.predictionNote: Just a rough estimate – on race day, how you feel, the course and the weather all count.
events.deleteRaceText: The race and its plan will be removed.
events.recalcText: Sessions from today on are created again. Past, completed and missed sessions stay as they are.
events.noWeeklyPlan: This programme doesn’t have a weekly plan yet.

session.sameDayHint: “{title}” is already on that day – that makes two sessions on the same day.
session.hardBefore: The day before has “{title}” (challenging) – plan an easy day or recovery.
session.missedHint: “{title}” – the reason helps you spot overload later on.
session.protectedDay: Your day – you can reschedule or skip this session and it won’t count against you. If you train anyway, you earn a bonus badge 🥊.
session.overdue: This session is in the past. You can still log it, reschedule it or mark it as missed.
session.restText: Recovery is part of training. Give your body a break.
session.noData: This session is marked as done, but no data was logged.
session.tooFastEasy: Too fast for an easy session
session.compareSub: Planned vs. actual for this session
session.needDurationOrDistance: Please enter a duration or distance
session.balanceText: To keep your load similar, you can take a comparable session out of the plan:
session.balanceNote: Just a suggestion – it’s your call. “Keep both” leaves everything as it is.
session.splitsBarHint: Bars: ±30 s around your average kilometre
session.exercisesIntroUsage: Sorted by how often you use them. Tap one to see the follow-along animation; ticked exercises count when you complete the session.
session.routeNoMap: Drawn without a map – your route stays on your server.
session.loadSrcFlat: no duration, so counted as 30 minutes
session.hardAfter: The day after has “{title}” (challenging) – plan an easy day or recovery.

offsetWeekKm.other: That makes {count} sessions this week ({km} km).

plans.paceAmbitious: Your target time {time} is ambitious: it equals VDOT {goal}, while your current form is VDOT {form}. So you train at your current form, and race pace follows the target time. {base}
plans.paceFromGoalAndForm: Target paces from your target time and your form (VDOT {vdot}): {base}
plans.paceFromGoal: Target paces from your target time {time} (VDOT {vdot}): {base}
plans.paceFromForm: Target paces from your current form (VDOT {vdot}): {base}
plans.paceFromZones: Target paces from your training zones: {base}
plans.history: Your last four weeks: {week}{longest}. The plan picks up from there.
plans.commitCopyHint: As in the plan “{name}”: {summary} Dates that are already there won’t show up twice.
plans.commitChangeHint: {summary} – you can change them under “Fixed commitments” in the plan.
plans.adaptedToForm: Adapted to your form: the build-up starts at your current long-run level of {km}.
plans.paceNone: Without a target time or hard runs there are no pace targets yet – add a target time or run a test (e.g. 5 km at a brisk pace), and the target paces will follow.
plans.historyNone: No runs logged in the last few weeks yet – so the plan starts gently.
plans.updateIntro: Sessions from today on are recalculated with the current plan logic: race session on race day, target paces from your target time, volume to match your level and run days. Past and completed sessions stay as they are.
plans.setupIntro: A few details so the plan fits you. You can change everything later.
plans.triathlonNote: Triathlon (beta): a fixed weekly structure with a rest day on Monday – two swim, two bike and three run sessions, taper and race format.
plans.hyroxNote: Hyrox (beta): a fixed weekly structure with two rest days – run intervals, strength, station training up to a race simulation, taper.
plans.commitEditHint: Once the plan is created, you can pick your dates.
plans.commitNoneHint: The plan can use every day. You can add fixed dates at any time.
plans.commitQuestion: Do you have fixed commitments, such as club training or matches? The plan then works around them.
plans.cannotCreate: No plan can be created for this date
plans.commitActionHint: Football, classes – the plan works around them
plans.toCalendarHint: All sessions as a calendar file
plans.noPlanText: There’s no training plan for this goal yet.
plans.incompleteText: This training plan has no phase structure (for example from an older backup).
plans.newLogicText: Race session on any weekday, target paces from your target time, volume to match your level and run days. If you like, the app recalculates your plan from today – the past stays as it is.
plans.commitEditorIntro: Fixed commitments (e.g. club training) are locked into the plan – the training plan works around them. When you save, the plan is recalculated from today; the past stays as it is.
plans.footballIntensityHint: Football is especially demanding – the intensity sets how much the session counts towards load & form and whether the coach suggests an easier next day.
plans.triagePriority: When sessions clash, the app prioritises: fixed commitments → key runs (time goal) → strength → easy volume.
plans.regenProgramText: Sessions from today on are created afresh. Past, completed and missed sessions stay as they are.
plans.levelLineBase: · starting from your current volume (avg {km} km a week)
plans.regenWeekFresh: This week’s planned sessions will be created afresh.
plans.regenWeekFreshFromToday: This week’s planned sessions from today on will be created afresh.

regenWeekKept.one: {count} session you’ve already done is kept.
regenWeekKept.other: {count} sessions you’ve already done are kept.

plans.regenWeekLost: Moves and manual changes in this week will be lost.

commitments.footballTrainingDesc: Team training – counts as cross-training (sprints, speed, joy of the game). Warm up well – for example with the FIFA 11+ football warm-up from the exercise library – then jog easy for 5–10 min. If it was intense, take your next run a little easier.
commitments.matchDesc: League or cup match – a high, race-like load. Keep the day after deliberately easy or rest; the training week is built around it.

rolling.reasonAcwr: Your last 7 days were clearly harder than planned and than your average over the weeks before (ratio {ratio}).

reasonStreak.one: {count} hard day in a row, more than planned – a calm day gives your body time to adapt.
reasonStreak.other: {count} hard days in a row, more than planned – a calm day gives your body time to adapt.

rolling.reasonFatigue: More load than planned (ratio {ratio}) and clearly tired – your fatigue is well above your fitness.
rolling.recoveryDesc: Deliberately easy – today your body needs recovery, not a training stimulus. Keep it very gentle in Z1, or go for a walk. Do the hard session later, once you’re more rested.
rolling.gentleDesc: Deliberately calm – recovery instead of stimulus.

dualgoal.noteBase: Base phase – the ideal time to lose weight: a moderate deficit with plenty of easy volume.
dualgoal.noteBuild: Build phase – hard sessions need energy: a smaller deficit and plenty of protein to keep their quality up.
dualgoal.notePeak: Peak phase – performance comes first: keep the deficit small, or the quality of your sessions suffers.
dualgoal.noteTaper: Taper – refuel now instead of losing weight: eat well so you’re fit for race day.
dualgoal.stimulusEnough: Your training gives you enough stimulus for real progress.
dualgoal.stimulusLow: Not much challenging stimulus lately – rest days alone won’t bring you closer to your goal. Plan key sessions again (stimulus + recovery = progress).

overdue.other: {count} sessions are waiting to be made up

dashboard.overdueHint: Move it, log it late or mark it as missed.
dashboard.restDayText: No session planned – enjoy the rest.

dashboard.stepGoal: Set up a goal or programme

dashboard.stepMembersHint: Family or team – everyone with their own PIN
dashboard.startIntro: Three quick steps, then Cat-O-Fit plans with you.

dashboardCoach.volumeText: This week {missed} km were left undone ({done}/{planned} km done). Add some of it gently to your next easy session – without doubling up the load.
dashboardCoach.rpeText: Average RPE {rpe} out of 10 from {count} rated sessions over the last {weeks} weeks.
dashboardCoach.restWholeText: {reason} That day ({date}) has {count} sessions from your goals – the whole day goes easy so the recovery really works.
dashboardCoach.restText: {reason} Suggestion: turn “{title}” on {date} into a recovery day.

log.destackReason: “{title}” moved to a free day – no more two sessions on the same day.
log.autoRestDescription: Deliberately easy – the whole day is set to recovery (including a second session from your goals). You’ll make up the original load once you’re rested. Undo it under “Recent automatic adjustments”.
log.footballReason: Football was demanding – next session eased.
log.deloadReason: Load has been high for a while.
log.boostReason: Room to spare lately – a little more volume.

dashboardCoach.restWholeToast: Whole day eased – {count} sessions set to easy
dashboardCoach.footballText: Football takes a lot out of you. Take “{title}” on {date} a bit easier – you’ll be fresher for the key sessions.
dashboardCoach.destackText: {date}: “{keep}” and “{move}” from your goals fall on the same day. Moving “{move}” to {weekday} ({target}) spreads the day out – each session gets its stimulus and recovery works.
dashboardCoach.readinessText: Today’s plan is “{title}” – a demanding one. With low readiness, an easy session often does more than a forced hard one.
dashboardCoach.makeupText: “{title}” from {date} was missed. {weekday} ({target}) is free – move it there?
dashboardCoach.undoneSkipped: Undone – sessions already done stay as they are
dashboardCoach.restPlannedToast: Recovery day planned – you’ll make up the session once you’re rested
dashboardCoach.footballToast: Made easier – you’ll do the key session when you’re fresher
dashboardCoach.destackToast: Day spread out – the session is now on a free day
dashboardCoach.easierToast: Made easier – key sessions come back once you’ve recovered
dashboardCoach.makeupToast: Key session rescheduled – it’s in your plan now
dashboardCoach.deloadToast: Lighter week on – less volume, more recovery
dashboardCoach.boostToast: Next week is a bit tougher – good luck!
dashboardCoach.rpeAskText: How it felt makes your load more accurate than any watch – one tap is enough.
dashboardCoach.matchText: These activities came from Apple Health or a file and fit planned sessions on the same day. Once matched, those sessions count as done – without counting the load twice.
dashboardCoach.returnTextInjured: On {date} you missed a session because of an injury. Start with easy sessions and build up step by step – hard sessions only once you feel fully fit again. You don’t need to make anything up. If the pain persists, have a doctor check it.
dashboardCoach.returnTextIll: On {date} you missed a session because you were ill. Start with easy sessions and build up step by step – hard sessions only once you feel fully fit again. You don’t need to make anything up.
dashboardCoach.deloadText: Your sessions over the last {weeks} weeks were very hard on average. A lighter week ({count} sessions with less volume, same intensity) helps you come back stronger. Fixed appointments stay as they are.
dashboardCoach.deloadTextRpe: Your sessions over the last {weeks} weeks were very hard on average (average RPE {rpe}). A lighter week ({count} sessions with less volume, same intensity) helps you come back stronger. Fixed appointments stay as they are.
dashboardCoach.boostText: Your sessions over the last {weeks} weeks were rather easy, and your load is in its usual range. If you like, add a little next week ({count} sessions) – about 12% more volume.
dashboardCoach.boostTextRpe: Your sessions over the last {weeks} weeks were rather easy (average RPE {rpe}), and your load is in its usual range. If you like, add a little next week ({count} sessions) – about 12% more volume.
dashboardCoach.rpeFromHr: Until then, estimated from heart rate: {rpe} out of 10
dashboardCoach.rpeFromType: Until then, the default for this sport counts: {rpe} out of 10
